name: Filipino Shrimp Fried Rice Noodles with Peas, Carrot, Tomato, Bok Choy & Cabbage (Two Ways)

ingredients.name: raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.

Fill a medium saucepan about halfway with hot water (from the tap), cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, remove from heat, uncover, and add rice noodles. Soak for 10 minutes (or prepare according to package instructions). Drain in a colander and set aside.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 baby bok choy
1 tomato
1 medium carrot
½ small bunch green onion (scallion)

instructions.primary_message: Trim and cut bok choy crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Small dice tomato. Place both in a medium bowl, along with shredded cabbage, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message: ½ (397 g) bag shredded cabbage (coleslaw mix)

instructions.primary_message: Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrot. Place on a plate and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

While the skillet heats up, if using frozen shrimp, place them in a colander and run under cold water to thaw them slightly and remove any ice crystals. (If using fresh shrimp, skip this step.) Place the shrimp on a clean towel or paper towels and pat dry.
instructions.secondary_message: 454 g raw peeled shrimp, fresh or frozen

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shrimp, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until just opaque, 2-3 minutes. Transfer 1 cup of shrimp to the plate with the carrot. Place remaining shrimp in a small bowl and set aside. (Reserve skillet for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp neutral vegetable oil
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Return skillet to medium-high heat, add more oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. Add peas, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes. Transfer a ½-cup of peas to the plate and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp neutral vegetable oil
1 ½ cups frozen peas
⅛ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add bok choy, tomato, and cabbage to the skillet with the remaining peas, then stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies have softened, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, roughly chop 1 cup of the cooked rice noodles. Add to the plate with the shrimp and veggies, then set aside.

Add remaining whole rice noodles to the skillet, along with reserved shrimp in the bowl, water, soy sauce, and fish sauce. Toss to combine, then continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until warmed through, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ cup water
soy sauce
1 tbsp fish sauce

instructions.primary_message: While the noodles are heating, place additional soy sauce and honey in another small bowl. Stir to combine the sweet soy sauce and set aside.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces.

FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide reserved grated carrot, plain shrimp, peas, and chopped noodles between plates. Drizzle noodles with sweet soy sauce.

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide shrimp noodle stir-fry between plates or bowls and top with green onions. Enjoy!
